title: Sell Mineral Rights in Dennison, OH
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Dennison, OH
metaDescription: Dennison sits in Tuscarawas County on the Utica flank, with a long Clinton sandstone legacy underneath. See what that mix means before you sell.
heroLead: Dennison grew up as a railroad town, and the mineral history under it is layered the same way, old Clinton-era wells sitting below whatever Utica flank potential a given tract might carry.
intro: Dennison sits in Tuscarawas County along the old Panhandle Route rail line, a small town whose mineral estates were mostly severed generations ago through farm and rail-adjacent land deals rather than modern oil and gas leasing. Being on the Utica flank rather than deep in the core belt to the east, drilling activity here has been lighter than in Harrison or Belmont counties, but this part of Tuscarawas has decades of shallower Clinton sandstone production that predates the shale conversation entirely.

sections.heading: Clinton legacy wells versus Utica flank potential
paragraphs: Most of the historical production around Dennison comes from Clinton sandstone wells, shallow, long-lived, low-volume producers that were common across Tuscarawas County well before horizontal Utica drilling existed. A deed that reserves 'oil and gas' broadly can cover both zones, so if you're holding minerals here, it's worth finding out whether your interest sits under an old Clinton well, a potential Utica unit, both, or neither, since that changes the value conversation entirely.

sections.heading: What ownership typically looks like around Dennison
paragraphs: A lot of mineral interests in this part of Tuscarawas County trace back to family farms split among children over multiple generations, which means small fractional interests are common. If your deed shows something like 'one-eighth of one-half interest,' that's a signal the tract has already been divided at least once, and a title search through the county recorder is the way to confirm your actual current decimal.

faqs.question: Is there active drilling right around Dennison?
faqs.answer: It's variable. Dennison sits on the flank of the Utica play, so development has been more selective here than in core counties further south, but the older Clinton sandstone has real production history in this area.

faqs.question: How do I find out which formation my mineral rights cover?
faqs.answer: Check the language in your original severance or reservation deed at the Tuscarawas County Recorder's office, and if you have a lease or royalty statement, that document will usually name the specific well and formation.

faqs.question: My family's interest has never been leased. Is it still worth anything?
faqs.answer: It can be, though an unleased interest with no nearby drilling activity is priced more conservatively than a producing one. Value depends on your net mineral acres and how much activity, if any, is happening on nearby units.

faqs.question: What documents should I gather before contacting a buyer?
faqs.answer: Your deed or the original severance instrument, any lease or division order, and recent royalty statements if you have them. Those three things let a buyer give you a real range instead of a guess.
